sourceExcerpt: Ad 1. Die ethische Gewissensynsur, Triebfaktor e, hat die besondere Aufgabe, durch eine durch das Gewissen unbewußt gelenkte Stellungnahme, die Gefahr von Aggression und Sadismus (Faktor s) abzuwehren.
romanianRendering: În dialectica Rand–Mitte, factorul e este descris de Szondi ca Gewissenszensur și primește sarcina specială de a lua, prin Gewissen, o poziție de apărare față de pericolul de Aggression und Sadismus atribuit factorului s.
doctrinalStatement: În modelul Rand–Mitte al lui Szondi, factorul e din Mitte are o relație funcțională specifică cu factorul s de la Rand: e este atribuit Stellungnahme/Abwehr față de Triebgefahr descrisă istoric în domeniul s ca Aggression/Sadismus. Această regulă stabilește axa interpretativă e↔s, dar nu stabilește, fără reacțiile concrete și fără suport suplimentar, dacă apărarea este activă, suficientă sau reușită într-un profil individual.
conditions: Use as a Rand–Mitte relational rule between factor e in the Mitte and factor s at the Rand.
The promoted rule is factor-level and does not by itself assign a sign-specific meaning to e or s.
exceptions: Do not infer successful inhibition, moral character, behavioral self-control or absence of aggression from the mere presence of factor e.
Do not infer actual aggression, violence, dangerousness, criminal behavior or a modern sadism diagnosis from the mere presence or reaction of factor s without separate source-grounded authorization.
Sign-specific execution requires a separately reviewed record; DR_SZ_TRIEBPATH_1_000003 supplies the clinician-admitted visual arbitration for the exact s +!! / e + example.
scopeNotes: Rand consists of S and C; Mitte consists of P and Sch in the source's functional topology.

The source uses historical terms such as Gewissenszensur, Aggression and Sadismus. They are retained as Szondian model terms and must not be silently modernized into contemporary diagnosis or factual behavior.
The sentence later contains hereditary language about factor e; that hereditary claim is not promoted by this doctrine record.
